incidents.victim: Daemon Tools users (government, science, manufacturing, retail in Russia, Belarus, Thailand)
incidents.vector: Trojanized Daemon Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate, distributed through the official website since at least April 8.
incidents.impact: Thousands of machines infected with a backdoor that exfiltrates host data; a more capable second-stage 'QUIC RAT' implant was selectively deployed against high-value targets including a Russian educational institution. Researchers found Chinese-language artifacts in the malware.

incidents.victim: Monterrey municipal water and drainage utility (Mexico)
incidents.vector: Hacker leveraged a large language model to conduct large portions of the intrusion, per incident-response firm Dragos.
incidents.impact: First publicly reported case of an AI-driven intrusion against a water utility; cited by CISA officials as evidence that AI is changing the speed of attacks against critical infrastructure.

incidents.victim: United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar)
incidents.vector: Surge of intrusion attempts, DDoS, and claimed compromises following the start of the 2026 conflict; Iran-aligned hacktivists, opportunistic criminals, and state-aligned actors using AI-assisted tooling.
incidents.impact: Daily breach attempts against the UAE rose from 90,000-200,000 to 600,000-800,000. UAE saw 15x normal cyber-relevant activity, Saudi Arabia 25x, Qatar 4x. Mix has shifted from defacement/DDoS boasts to claimed intrusions of finance, telecoms, aviation, and energy-adjacent infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Albertans (~3 million citizens, ~60% of provincial population)
incidents.vector: Activist group 'Centurion Project' is alleged to have obtained Alberta's list of electors without authorization.
incidents.impact: Police investigating unauthorized possession of voter list (names, addresses, personal info) ahead of an Alberta independence referendum. Source of the leak inside Elections Alberta is not yet identified.

incidents.victim: cPanel/WHM hosting customers (~15,000 compromised servers; ~1.5M instances exposed; ~70M domains served)
incidents.vector: Authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-41940 (CVSS 9.8) in cPanel/WHM/WP Squared; mass exploitation began within 24 hours of the April 28 patch, with confirmed in-the-wild abuse going back to Feb 23.
incidents.impact: Roughly 15,000 instances compromised in the first 24 hours; attackers deployed Mirai variants and a file-encrypting ransomware that appends '.sorry' to files. Full server takeover, MFA-bypass, and credential theft observed; researchers warn the bug is wormable.

incidents.victim: Linux servers worldwide (Ubuntu, RHEL, Debian, SUSE, Amazon Linux, AlmaLinux; kernels 4.14-6.19.12)
incidents.vector: Linux kernel logic flaw CVE-2026-31431 ('Copy Fail') in the algif_aead/AF_ALG cryptographic interface; a 732-byte Python script reliably escalates an unprivileged local user to root across distributions.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation in the wild; CISA added CVE-2026-31431 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Enables Kubernetes container escapes, multi-tenant host takeover, and CI/CD pipeline compromise. Hundreds of derivative AI-generated proof-of-concepts now circulating.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America (since late 2024) and southeastern Europe (since 2025)
incidents.vector: Suspected exploitation of zero-day/n-day vulnerabilities for initial access, followed by deployment of NetDraft (.NET FinalDraft variant), CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL with SNOWLIGHT/SNOWRUST stagers, and shared Chinese-speaking APT tooling.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos disclosed long-term access to government networks in two regions; tooling overlaps with multiple known Chinese-speaking APT clusters. Post-compromise activity included credential theft, Active Directory enumeration and lateral movement.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a portion of Trellix's source code repository.
incidents.impact: Trellix disclosed the breach on May 1 and engaged forensic experts and law enforcement. Company says no evidence build/release process or distribution was affected, but a source-code breach can expose detection logic and product internals to attackers.

incidents.victim: Instructure (Canvas LMS) — 9,000+ schools, universities and businesses
incidents.vector: Account/credential compromise; Instructure responded by revoking privileged credentials and access tokens. ShinyHunters group claimed responsibility on its leak site.
incidents.impact: Hackers accessed names, email addresses, student ID numbers and user messages. ShinyHunters claims 3.6 TB of data from 9,000+ schools. Instructure says no financial data, passwords, or government documents were stolen. Containment briefly disrupted Canvas tools used by customers.

incidents.vector: World Leaks group (rebrand of Hunters International) carried out a data-theft extortion operation against the publisher.
incidents.impact: 8.5 TB of allegedly sensitive files released on the dark web, including payroll, contracts, financial statements and editorial communications. Local outlets reported leaked material included a January 2025 editorial memo suggesting Mediaworks would 'contact Moscow for help' on articles discrediting Ukraine's Zelensky.

incidents.victim: Indian and Russian organizations (industrial, consulting, retail, transportation)
incidents.vector: Tax-themed phishing emails impersonating Indian and Russian tax authorities; archives delivered a Rust-based loader that staged ValleyRAT and the previously undocumented 'ABCDoor' Python backdoor.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky observed 1,600+ malicious messages between January and February 2026 from the Silver Fox group. Campaign expanded the actor's regional focus from Taiwan/Japan/North America to add Russia and India for the first time. ABCDoor provides screen streaming, remote input, clipboard theft and limited file encryption.

incidents.victim: 35,000+ users across 13,000 organizations in 26 countries (92% U.S.) — primarily Healthcare, Financial Services, Professional Services, Technology
incidents.vector: Multi-stage 'code of conduct' phishing emails with PDF attachments and fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs that funnel users into an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) Microsoft sign-in flow capturing session tokens.
incidents.impact: AiTM proxy intercepts authentication and steals session cookies, bypassing non-phishing-resistant MFA and giving attackers immediate Microsoft 365 account access. Microsoft Defender Research observed the campaign April 14-16, 2026.

incidents.vector: Mirai-based DDoS botnet built from TP-Link Archer AX21 routers vulnerable to CVE-2023-1389; attacks coordinated using SSH keys and infrastructure belonging to Brazilian DDoS-mitigation provider Huge Networks.
incidents.impact: Years of large-scale DDoS attacks against Brazilian ISPs traced to a botnet operating with stolen access to Huge Networks. Each target prefix attacked 10-60 seconds with four parallel processes per host. Huge Networks attributes the activity to a January 2026 intrusion of dev servers and CEO SSH keys; CEO denies sabotaging competitors.

incidents.victim: Delta Dental Insurance Company (DDIC) and Delta Dental of New York (DDNY)
incidents.vector: Mid-2023 exploitation of the MOVEit Transfer zero-day to access file-transfer servers used to share data with affiliates, partners, providers and employees.
incidents.impact: NYDFS announced a $2.25M settlement; threat actors exfiltrated names, addresses, SSNs, driver's license numbers, financial account info and patient health data. DFS faulted the companies for inadequate incident-response procedures and untimely cybersecurity-event reporting under 23 NYCRR Part 500.

incidents.victim: Julia Klöckner, President of the German Bundestag
incidents.vector: Compromise of Klöckner's Signal account, giving access to a sensitive group chat that also included Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
incidents.impact: Russian operators read messages in a sensitive group involving the German Chancellor; Merz's own account was not compromised. Part of an ongoing Russian campaign against Signal and WhatsApp accounts of senior European officials.

incidents.vector: Use of leaked contractor credentials and guessed Mythos endpoints to access the private agent on launch day.
incidents.impact: A group of AI hobbyists gained access to Anthropic's pre-release Mythos cybersecurity agent. Anthropic says intruders did not run malicious prompts and appeared to have only 'played around', but the incident underscores the contractor and credential-management risks of frontier AI rollouts.
